chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Sindi ibn Muhammad and Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who has a male slave who is a son of fornication, and he marries him to a female slave, and a child is born to them, is his child freed to seek the countenance of Allah, the Exalted? He said: 'Yes, there is no harm, let him free him if he wishes.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm, let him free him if he wishes.'

key_terms.وَلَدُ زِنًى: Son of fornication (a specific category of slave)
key_terms.يُلْتَمَسُ بِهِ وَجْهُ اللَّهِ: To seek the countenance/pleasure of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a slave who is a son of fornication and his children?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a slave who is a 'walad zina' (child of fornication) can be manumitted to seek God's pleasure, a ruling that underscores the spiritual merit of freeing those with distinct social statuses. This narration highlights the flexibility in Islamic jurisprudence regarding the emancipation of specific slave categories, encouraging voluntary manumission as an act of worship.
